data.name: Simeon
data.gender_notes: Simeon is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Hebrew name Shim'on, meaning 'God has heard.' In the Bible, Simeon is the name of two significant figures: one of the twelve tribes of Israel and the old man who recognized Jesus as the Messiah. The name Simeon carries the meaning “Obtained by God” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Simeon usually hope their child will grow to embody obtained by god and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Simeon belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Obtained by God.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Simeon total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: The name Simeon has been popular throughout history, particularly in Europe. In France alone, it was in the top 100 names from the 16th to the 19th centuries. It is also the name of several saints and notable figures.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christianity, the old man Simeon is considered a prophet and a just and devout man who was waiting for the coming of the Messiah. When he held the baby Jesus in his arms, he recognized Him as the long-awaited Savior. This event is commemorated in the feast day of the Presentation of the Lord (February 2). Simeon's faith and anticipation remind us of the importance of seeking and recognizing God in our lives.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Simeon, deriving from the Hebrew name Shim'on, means "hearing" or "obedient." In Christian tradition, Simeon is the righteous elder who, guided by the Holy Spirit, recognizes and reverences the infant Jesus as the long-awaited Messiah.
